top.title: NYT bestseller ‘Robopocalypse’ is getting a TV series with Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman at the helm
top.description: null They say all good things come to those who wait… and WAIT. Well, the wait for "Robopocalypse" fans might finally be over, as Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman have announced they're working on a TV adaptation. It does seem like an eternity since news first broke that Portland-based New York Times bestselling author Daniel H. Wilson’s "Robopocalypse" (Doubleday, 2011) was bought by Steven Spielberg’s DreamWorks SKG for a sci-fi spectacle, with Drew Goddard ("The Martian") brought in to pen the screenplay. That was back in 2009, and since then the story of a rogue AI named Archos and a hearty band of indigenous people in America’s heartland battling to save humanity from extinction has been placed on Hollywood’s back burner. After numerous stalled starts and director Michael Bay getting involved in 2018, "Robopocalypse" was quietly powered down due to script issues, filmmaker scheduling conflicts, and the enormous budget required. But now we have been blessed with the news , first broken by The Hollywood Reporter, that Ron Howard ("Apollo 13," "The Da Vinci Code") and Akiva Goldsman ("A Beautiful Mind," "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds") have taken up the mantle of this chilling sci-fi project to develop as a new TV series. And what timing, just as AI fever has gripped the planet with paranoia centered around our eventual robot overlords. "'Robopocalypse' has all the scale and suspense of a major action story, but what drew me to it are the thought-provoking themes and humanity at its center," Ron Howard shared in a statement. Wilson Vintage "Daniel created a future that feels both startling and increasingly plausible, with characters who must figure out what connects us when the technology we rely on turns against us. I am also thrilled to work with Akiva again. We have shared some incredibly meaningful creative experiences, and this feels like the right story to bring us back together." As a PhD graduate of Carnegie Mellon University’s Robotics Institute and a future king of the techno-thriller, Wilson was the ideal writer to bring this frightening story to life, and a 2014 sequel titled "Robogenesis" was equally gripping. The prolific, award-winning writer has since set up a multitude of other Hollywood projects spawned from his catalog of works, including "Amped," "The Clockwork Dynasty," the authorized sequel to Michael Crichton's "The Andromeda Strain," " The Andromeda Evolution ," and his 2025 alien invasion novel "Hole in the Sky," still alive at Netflix. top.title: FG suspends broadcast licence fee reviews indefinitely
top.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has suspended all reviews of broadcast licence fees indefinitely following concerns by operators over rising operational costs and financial pressures facing Nigeria’s broadcasting industry. The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, announced the decision on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by a delegation of the Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria (BON), led by its Chairman, Senior High Chief Dr Tony Akiotu. The decision followed BON’s 82nd General Assembly in Calabar, Cross River State, where the organisation raised concerns about the sustainability of broadcast operations amid mounting economic challenges. In a statement issued on Monday night by the Minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Rabiu Ibrahim, Idris said the suspension was part of efforts by the Federal Government to create a more conducive operating environment for broadcasters. “Any increase in licence fees is hereby put on hold. All reviews relating to licences are suspended until further notice. I am directing the NBC to ensure strict compliance while we review the situation,” he said. The minister also directed the Director-General of the National Broadcasting Commission (NBC) to expedite the review of the National Broadcasting Code to ensure that its provisions reflect current developments and emerging realities in the industry. On the Digital Switch-Over (DSO) programme, Idris promised to convene a stakeholders’ meeting to address outstanding concerns and resolve challenges affecting its implementation. He further disclosed that he had directed the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON) to ensure full enforcement of the 45-day payment period for advertising services, following BON’s request for improved compliance with the policy. The minister also assured the delegation that the ministry would engage relevant stakeholders on concerns surrounding access to affordable financing and spectrum allocation. Describing broadcasting as critical to national development, Idris said the industry played an important role in strengthening democracy, promoting national cohesion and ensuring public access to credible and accurate information. With the 2027 general elections approaching, he urged broadcasters to uphold professionalism, fairness and ethical standards in their reportage. “Freedom of expression must go with responsibility. You cannot simply say anything and claim to be practising journalism. “Journalism has standards, procedures and ethics. I urge broadcasters to ensure that what they report is factual, responsible and promotes national unity and peaceful coexistence,” the minister said. Earlier, BON Chairman, Akiotu, commended Idris for his intervention during the June 2026 DSO launch, noting that the stakeholders’ meeting convened by the minister helped address concerns about ensuring a level playing field for operators. After months and months of deliberation, it’s official. The College Football Playoff will be expanding to 24 teams starting in 2027. That makes 2026 the final-year of the 12-team playoff, and the race for those spots is really starting to heat up after an eventful Week 10 on Saturday. But what would happen if the 24-team playoff were being implemented this season? The biggest shift is that, in the future era of the 24-team field, conference championship games are being eliminated. top.title: Blades Brown’s Win Proves 19-year-olds Can Beat The Best Right Now
top.description: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images Golf history just got rewritten by a teenager who refused to quit. Blades Brown, just 19 years old, captured his first PGA Tour title on Sunday in Mexico. He did something no one has done in 95 years. The win came after he erased a seven-stroke deficit in the final round against Ben James. This isn’t just a lucky break for a kid. It is a statement that the future of the game is here and it is aggressive. The Comeback That Shocked Everyone Most players would have folded with that kind of hole in the standings. Brown did not even blink. He closed with a nine-under 63 to force a playoff, according to the Associated Press. The final score was 23-under 265, which cleared a logjam of eight players who were all within a single stroke of one another. On the second sudden-death hole, a four-foot birdie putt secured the victory for him. Brown is now the fourth-youngest winner in tour history. He bypassed college entirely to turn pro out of high school, a move that paid off instantly. “It hasn’t set in just yet, I guess, the magnitude of being a PGA Tour winner,” Brown said in a statement reported by Yahoo Sports . That lack of shock is exactly what makes this win so dangerous for the rest of the field. He has been thinking about this day since he was five years old. Now he is living it. At the 2023 U.S. Amateur, the kid broke a 103-year-old record, joining Tiger Woods as the only players to win the U.S. Junior Amateur and be the medalist in the U.S. Amateur in the same year. Success at this age is not an accident. Why The Old Guard Should Worry Ben James fought hard but fell short. James held a four-shot lead after 54 holes before the game got away from him on Sunday. He still managed to force the playoff with a clutch eagle on the 18th hole. James hit a 285-yard shot into 20 feet and made the putt to salvage a 70. “Had a feeling that it was going to go in,” James said of his eagle putt, per the Associated Press. But he missed an eight-foot putt on the second playoff hole while Brown made his three-footer. Last season, James held the number one spot in the PGA Tour University ranking, but he failed to stop the younger talent. The combined age of these two players in the playoff was 42, the youngest in tour history. This signals a shift in who wins on Sunday. A Masters berth is nearer for Brown at 54th globally, provided he ends the season within the top 50. Brown said with a huge grin, according to Yahoo Sports, “I’m just so obsessed with this game,”. That obsession is the difference maker. That obsession proves experience does not always beat hunger when the pressure is highest.

top.description: Everton make decision on Jack Grealish amid Man City return rumours Everton Stand Firm on Jack Grealish Loan as David Moyes Awaits Response Everton have reached a clear internal position on Jack Grealish, with no intention at present of cutting short his loan from Manchester City, despite renewed scrutiny around the winger’s situation. As first reported by TeamTalk , club sources continue to indicate that David Moyes and Everton are prepared to keep backing the 31-year-old, while expecting a visible response during training over the international break. The latest developments follow a difficult spell for Grealish, who has missed Everton’s last four matches. The first absence came through illness, though wider attention has centred on off-field disciplinary issues and the resulting speculation over whether the club could return him to City ahead of schedule. That is not the direction Everton are currently taking. Instead, the expectation is that Grealish will rejoin the group at Finch Farm during the break, with the focus firmly on attitude, sharpness and a route back into contention before Everton’s trip to Brentford on Monday 23 November. It is understood that the player has been reminded privately of his responsibilities, a message that underlines both support and accountability. David Moyes keeping faith in Jack Grealish There is still a strong belief inside Everton that Grealish can play a major role if he rediscovers rhythm and focus. His return of eight goal involvements in 22 games last season offered enough evidence of what he can bring when fully engaged, and that remains part of the thinking behind the club’s decision not to make a drastic move. The situation is also being framed by the team’s recent results. Everton have won three matches without him, which has strengthened competition for places and reduced any sense of dependency. That helps Moyes, who now has leverage as much as he has a selection issue. Grealish is not being written off, but he is being asked to earn his way back. Former Everton defender Michael Ball made that point clearly while also arguing that the club should work to maximise the player’s strengths. He said: “Last season, he was our key player. Recently, Everton have won three games without him, which should give the rest of the squad confidence.” Photo IMAGO Best role for Grealish at Everton Ball’s most interesting observation centred on positioning. top.title: Kyle Whittingham Reveals What Finally Convinced Him to Fire Jason Beck
top.description: Michigan Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham has finally revealed exactly what pushed him to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck , and apparently, it took one final look at the film to seal the deal. Speaking to reporters on Monday, Whittingham explained that he initially planned to wait until the conclusion of the 2026 season before making any major changes to his offensive coaching staff. However, after reviewing the film from Michigan’s embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State, he realized waiting was no longer an option. According to Brad Galli of WXYZ-TV , Whittingham pointed directly to the regression he witnessed against the Spartans as the reason for his sudden change of heart. The Michigan head coach also made something else perfectly clear: Nobody pressured him into firing Beck. Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham looks up at the scoreboard during second half action at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Michigan State won the game 15-6. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kyle Whittingham Reveals What Changed His Mind About Jason Beck During Monday’s press conference, Whittingham explained that watching Saturday’s game on film convinced him that an immediate coaching change was necessary. “When I turned the film on and really dove into it, it just became apparent to me that I needed to make the change now, and there’s just too much regression in the offense in that particular game, and that’s what led to the decision,” Whittingham said. That explanation is particularly interesting considering what Whittingham said immediately following Saturday’s loss. At the time, he suggested he would evaluate his coaching staff after the season rather than make an immediate change. But apparently, the film told a different story. Whittingham also addressed whether outside pressure played any role in his decision to part ways with Beck, who followed him from Utah to Michigan. “ Zero outside influence. Just my own analysis, my own feel, my own gut instinct ,” Whittingham said. Those comments leave little room for interpretation. Despite growing frustration among Michigan fans and mounting criticism of the offense, Whittingham insists the decision was entirely his own. Michigan’s Offensive Struggles Became Impossible to Ignore The numbers from Saturday’s loss to Michigan State were nothing short of disastrous for the Wolverines. Michigan managed just 192 total yards, including 54 rushing yards, while turning the ball over four times and allowing five sacks. Following the loss, Whittingham had already admitted the offense had taken three steps backward . His comments suggested he understood just how poorly Michigan had performed, but they did not indicate that a coaching change was imminent. top.title: Guardians’ Rule-5 Draft Prep for Fall 2026
top.description: OSU pitcher Justin Campbell leads the Big 12 with 39 strikeouts this season. cutout | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Theoretically, the Guardians will be adding some prospects to their 40-man roster ahead of the November 20th deadline to do so. Who are the top candidates to get the good news? There are a fair amount of complicating factors to this year’s Rule-5 draft, in which players who signed at 18 years or younger and have been in a professioanl organization for five years or players who signed at 19 or older and have spent for years in a professional organization become eligible for any team to take if they are willing to add them to their 26-man roster and keep them there for a full season (or return them to their original team, if not). There will not be a Rule-5 draft in December due to the impending lockout to be imposed by MLB owners on the first of that month. Will there be one prior to the 2027 season, if there is one? There wasn’t a Rule-5 draft prior to the last season impacted by a lockout. Finally, are their players the Guardians will have to balance their desire to add them to the roster vs. the risk of them not being able to play in the minor leagues in 2027 if they are, indeed, added? Everyone on the 40-man roster will be unable to participate in minor-league play during a lockout. I think the Guardians, and most MLB teams, will proceed as if there is going to be a Rule-5 draft because taking the risk that there will not be one is a big one when talking about the most valuable assets a team possesses – young, controllable talent. If you need a reminder of which Guardians’ prospects are eligible to be selected, I recommend TJStats excellent resource here . With that said, here are the players I believe the Guardians will add, and why: Very Likely Adds : Justin Campbell, RHP, 25 years-old – Campbell was one of the few bright spots in the Guardians’ minor league starting pitching last season with a 10.8/4.3 K/BB/9 and a 3.03 FIP, mostly at Columbus. Campbell did have a leg injury later in the year but still threw just short of 70 innings. top.description: The New York Giants are preparing for their Week 10 matchup on Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, but the league has made some changes to their schedule for the following week. This puts the Giants front and center for the national TV game of the week on Sunday afternoon. nigeria.title: Court dismisses Maihaja’s suit against Wali’s APC ticket
nigeria.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu A Federal High Court sitting in Damaturu, Yobe State, has dismissed a suit challenging the emergence of Alhaji Baba Malam Wali as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 general election. The suit was instituted by Engr. Mustapha Yunusa Maihaja, an aspirant in the party’s May 21 governorship primary, who alleged irregularities and non-compliance with the APC’s electoral guidelines. In a judgment delivered on Monday, November 9, 2026, Justice Fatima Murtala Amin held that the suit was statute-barred, having been filed outside the legally prescribed timeframe. The court also found that Maihaja failed to establish his allegations, particularly the claim of over-voting during the governorship primary. Justice Amin upheld a preliminary objection challenging the competence of the suit, thereby dismissing the case on procedural grounds. On the substantive issues, the judge identified material contradictions and inconsistencies in the testimonies of the plaintiff’s witnesses, describing the evidence as unreliable and insufficient to support the allegations. The court further held that even if the suit had been filed within the prescribed timeframe, it would still have failed on its merits because the plaintiff did not provide credible evidence to establish the alleged over-voting. Wali emerged winner of the APC governorship primary with 236,711 votes, securing the party’s ticket for the 2027 governorship election in the state. Reacting to the judgment, Wali’s Press Secretary, Shuaibu Abdullahi, commended the court for its consideration of the issues raised in the suit. “We commend the Court for its painstaking consideration of the issues and reaffirm our confidence in the judiciary as the ultimate guardian of justice and the rule of law,” Abdullahi said. The judgment dismisses the legal challenge to Wali’s emergence as the APC governorship candidate, leaving his party ticket intact ahead of the 2027 general election. nigeria.title: Barcelona teenager Pau Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy Award
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, becoming the first defender since Matthijs de Ligt in 2018 to receive the honour. The 19-year-old was recognised after a standout year with Barcelona and Spain. He helped Barça win a second consecutive LaLiga title and was part of Spain’s World Cup-winning team in North America, where he was named Young Player of the Tournament. “I’m very proud to receive the award, and I thank all the people who voted for me,” Cubarsí said in a video broadcast by Tuttosport at the ceremony. “It’s been a spectacular year, and we’re going for more,” he added. Cubarsí told Reuters that defenders can struggle to attract the same attention as attacking players. “It’s harder for defenders to get recognition… we’re less in the spotlight,” he said. “Perhaps our work isn’t as visible because, at the end of the day, the forwards score lots of goals, provide assists, play a more attractive style of football, are more eye-catching.” Spain conceded only one goal in eight matches en route to winning the World Cup, and Cubarsí played a key role in the team’s defence. He becomes the fourth Barcelona player to win the men’s award in the last six years, following teammates Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal. Previous winners include Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland. The Golden Boy award, established by Italian newspaper Tuttosport in 2003, recognises the best under-21 player in a top European division. Journalists vote from a shortlist of nominees. nigeria.title: Man Utd delay decision on Carrick’s future after dropping into relegation zone — report
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United are not in a hurry to sack head coach Michael Carrick despite their drop into the Premier League relegation zone following Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, according to Sky Sports . Sky Sports News reports that the club’s hierarchy plan to use the international break to assess the team’s poor start to the season and reconsider their options before making a decision on Carrick’s future. The former United midfielder is under increasing pressure after the club recorded just one win in 11 matches, conceded 30 goals in all competitions and endured what has been described as their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. United’s 4-4 draw against Villa followed another comeback in their previous match, but the recent results have not been enough to ease concerns over their overall performances. Carrick and his players were given Monday off after the Villa encounter, with the head coach and his staff expected to return to the club’s Carrington training base on Tuesday. With several players away on international duty and no first-team training sessions scheduled in the coming days, the break is expected to give the club’s leadership time to conduct a broader review. According to Sky Sports, three major factors have contributed to the hierarchy’s decision not to rush a change in the dugout. First, United supporters have not called for Carrick to be dismissed, with the former midfielder still enjoying considerable affection from the fanbase because of his achievements as a player. Carrick won 11 major trophies during his playing career at Old Trafford, including the Champions League and five Premier League titles. Secondly, the club’s hierarchy believe the 45-year-old still has the support of the dressing room, despite the team’s poor form. The recent comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in the Premier League are understood to have reinforced the belief that the players have not given up on their manager. Thirdly, United’s decision-makers are reportedly not convinced that replacing Carrick would automatically resolve the team’s problems, with the performances of the players also under scrutiny. The report adds that the club could consider available managerial options, including Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe, if they eventually decide to make a change. For now, however, United are expected to take their time before deciding whether Carrick remains the right man to lead the club out of their current crisis. nigeria.title: Joe Biden scales back book tour as cancer ‘slows me down’
nigeria.description: Former US president Joe Biden says he is scaling back plans to promote his upcoming memoir as he battles aggressive prostate cancer, acknowledging that the illness sometimes leaves him struggling. The 83-year-old Democrat, whose health was a major issue during his presidency, said Sunday that he would be unable to make as many public appearances as he had hoped ahead of the November 17 release of “Promise Me, America.” “Some days are better than others. It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down,” Biden wrote on X. “What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves.” Biden announced in May 2025, four months after leaving the White House, that he had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had spread to his bones. He has since undergone radiation and hormone therapy, while his son Hunter said in August that the disease had spread further and was causing considerable pain. Biden struck an optimistic note about his treatment, saying his doctors “continue to be encouraged” by his response. His memoir chronicles his four years in the White House, including his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic, wars in Afghanistan and Ukraine, and his controversial decision to seek reelection in 2024 before withdrawing. In an excerpt published Monday by The Atlantic, Biden delivered a blistering attack on his successor Donald Trump over the 2021 assault on the US Capitol by supporters seeking to overturn Trump’s election defeat. “What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave,” Biden wrote. He also recalled an unexpectedly friendly Oval Office meeting with Trump following the Republican’s 2024 election victory, during which his successor suggested they might have been friends outside politics. Biden abandoned his reelection campaign in July 2024 after a disastrous debate against Trump intensified concerns about his age and fitness for office. His vice president, Kamala Harris, subsequently lost the election, returning Trump to the White House. Biden said his book would explain the decisions he made in office and reflect his faith in American democracy. nigeria.title: Why getting most votes is not enough to become Nigeria’s president
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – No candidate can become Nigeria’s president simply by polling the highest number of votes. The 1999 Constitution also demands that the winner shows support across the federation. Read Also: * What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? * 2027: What happens when Nigerian election results are disputed? Also, there is no fixed number of votes that guarantees victory in presidential. Neither 10 million nor 15 million votes means anything on its own. Two conditions are set out in Section 134(2) of the Constitution. A candidate must first have “the highest number of votes cast at the election.” The second condition is the spread. The candidate must have “not less than one-quarter of the votes cast at the election in each of at least two-thirds of all the states in Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.” Nigeria has 36 states, and two-thirds of 36 is 24. The arithmetic is less settled once the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, is counted as a 37th unit, because two-thirds of 37 is about 24.7. Lawyer Femi Falana (SAN) read the provision as meaning “25 states or 24 states plus the FCT”. The Constitution itself says in Section 2(2) that “Nigeria shall be a Federation consisting of States and a Federal Capital Territory.” In 2023 and 1979 The question of whether 25 per cent in Abuja is a separate, compulsory test went to the Supreme Court after the 2023 election. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, and Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, argued that Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, had failed it. Tinubu scored about 20 per cent in the FCT, while Obi won the territory. The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, argued that by scoring 25 per cent of the valid votes cast in 29 states, Tinubu had already met the constitutional requirement for presidential election. On Thursday, 26th October 2023, a Supreme Court panel led by Justice Inyang Okoro upheld the lower court’s ruling. The justices held that the FCT has no special status above the states. Under that ruling, 25 per cent in Abuja is not a standalone condition for victory. Section 299 of the Constitution, which treats the FCT as a state, was central to the reasoning. The arithmetic has been fought over before. In 1979, Obafemi Awolowo argued that two-thirds of the then 19 states meant 13 states, and that Shehu Shagari had reached 25 per cent in only 12. The Supreme Court settled that dispute by concluding it would be “12 two-thirds”. That meant 25 per cent in 12 states and 25 per cent of two-thirds of a 13th. When no one meets condition… What happens when nobody meets both conditions is also spelt out in Section 134. INEC must, within seven days of the result, arrange a run-off between two candidates. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot North Korean launderers are creating their own worthless meme coins and pushing stolen Binance funds through them so the coins never move directly from one wallet to another, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said Monday. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the operators minted at least six new tokens on the NEAR blockchain — named FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU — paired each with NEAR in its own liquidity pool, then bought the tokens with stolen NEAR and sold them back out through a second set of wallets. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Elliptic’s wider update now puts roughly 3,000 BTC — about $225 million — in new bitcoin addresses converted from other stolen assets, while about 11.8 million NEAR, or $43.7 million, from the theft has still not moved. “Most people think of meme tokens as joke coins whose prices rise and fall on hype,” Elliptic co-founder and chief scientist Dr. Tom Robinson wrote. “North Korea’s launderers have found a different use for them.” How the homemade token trick works The technique is a four-step hop. The North Korea launderers create a token with a public launch tool, open a liquidity pool pairing it with a real asset such as NEAR or a stablecoin, buy the new token with stolen funds from one set of wallets, then sell it back into the same pool from a second set of wallets that collect the real asset. At no point do the stolen funds transfer directly from a buying wallet to a collecting wallet, because the pool sits in between. To a casual observer, the collecting wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit. Each of the six NEAR tokens cost about 25 NEAR, or around $90, to create. Each was traded heavily within hours using stolen NEAR and then abandoned. None has traded since Nov. 8, and that afternoon the creators of four of them withdrew what liquidity was left. Five of the six token creators were funded by a wallet that had just sold an earlier token, between two and 13 minutes before the next launch, so the tokens form a chain. Elliptic first reported the same approach in the laundering of the February 2025 Bybit theft, also attributed to North Korean group TraderTraitor, when a worthless Tron token helped move at least $24 million. In the Binance case the firm has also seen the technique on Tron and a close variant on Solana that used existing thinly traded tokens rather than homemade ones. A slowing tactic, not a disappearing act The meme coins do not hide the funds. Every step is public on-chain. What they buy is time. The issue is whether exchanges and other platforms can offer yield or rewards to investors who keep dollar-pegged stablecoins on their platforms. Seiberg views action as unlikely, though he sees a “narrow path” for a ban. His rationale is procedural as much as political: it may be easier to find 60 Senate votes on stablecoin yield alone than on the broader crypto market structure bill, which failed a cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and which he already called effectively dead for this Congress after the Democratic midterm sweep. A ban, he wrote, would benefit banks. He expects them to renew the push in the next Congress on the theory that Democratic wins open a path. Why Seiberg still sees a path That path rests on a shift in the Senate. Key crypto advocates retired or lost, while skeptics are being elevated. Sen. Elizabeth Warren is likely to chair the Banking Committee, and Sen. Sherrod Brown, a longtime critic of the industry, regained his Ohio seat after crypto-backed spending of about $64 million failed to stop him, Seiberg wrote before the votes were counted. It is not his base case. Crypto politics are “complex,” he wrote, which is why the probability starts at 10%. Some Democrats will resist treating stablecoin yield outside a broader package. Seiberg again sees no path for the Clarity Act, arguing Democrats will insist on ethics and investor-protection provisions President Trump would reject. That split, he wrote, makes Democrats unlikely to unite behind a yield-only bill. Democrats are not united on the substance either. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, a lead Democrat on crypto policy, has backed paying rewards for using stablecoins rather than for passively holding them, a distinction that shaped the Tillis-Alsobrooks compromise text during Clarity talks. There is also a perception problem. Congress would be asked to stop voters from earning a return on stablecoin holdings even though they can earn one on savings accounts and money market funds. Seiberg questions whether Democratic leaders want a vote that could be framed as taking money from retail investors. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT Large bitcoin holders are swapping coins they guard themselves for shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) at a record pace, the firm’s head of digital assets said Monday, as kidnappings and hacks push security to the top of their list. “The current moment is the highest we’ve seen at any point,” Robbie Mitchnick told Barron’s , adding that demand for the swaps “has sort of been one way — up.” Of all the reasons clients give, he said, “the single largest one is security and peace of mind.” The trades are in-kind conversions. A holder delivers bitcoin to the fund through an intermediary and receives newly created IBIT shares, without first selling the coins for cash. BlackRock relies on Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to handle the transactions, and those firms set the minimum size. Barron’s put the volume BlackRock has seen at $3.6 billion, noting the real figure could be larger because the firm does not process every conversion itself. Mitchnick cited a bigger number in August, telling Bloomberg that IBIT had facilitated more than $5 billion of such swaps, up from more than $3 billion in October 2025 . In that August interview, BlackRock’s Mitchnick named the threats outright: “People see things happen in the outside world — whether it’s kidnappings, ransom, custody failures — that motivate them to make this switch for all or some of their holdings.” He told Barron’s the recent Binance hack was not news to big holders. “Most large Bitcoin holders were already acutely aware of the risk of holding on an exchange and in a hot wallet,” he said. How BlackRock’s swaps became possible The SEC voted on July 29, 2025, to let spot bitcoin and ether funds create and redeem shares in kind, ending the cash-only structure it required when the funds launched in January 2024. Access has widened since. BlackRock’s minimum started around $30 million and now hovers between $1 million and $2 million, Barron’s reported. Taxes are part of the pitch. Converting appreciated bitcoin into IBIT in kind “generally isn’t seen as a sale that would trigger capital-gains taxes,” Barron’s wrote, while Bloomberg cautioned that avoiding an immediate bill depends on the investor’s circumstances. Mitchnick also pointed to estate planning, calling it “much, much simpler” to hold the exposure “within the confines of their private bank.” Once inside, the coins sit with IBIT’s custodian, an affiliate of Coinbase Prime, in what Mitchnick called an “institutional-grade cold-storage model.” The fund held 795,921 BTC, worth about $60.4 billion, as of Nov. 6. A Binance spokesperson confirmed to CoinDesk the closure date over the weekend, saying the exchange is “progressively restricting certain services for affected users” now that the transition period under the Markets in Crypto-Assets framework has ended. “Affected accounts will be closed with effect from 31 December 2026,” the spokesperson said, calling it “a carefully managed process.” Binance said customer assets remain safe and accessible and described the move as “no sudden freeze.” Deposits are already blocked, but users can still withdraw crypto and fiat. Users in the four countries have shared the notices on X. The fees and deadlines According to emails that users shared, Binance will charge 0.025% of remaining crypto balances each month, or 10 USDC, whichever is higher, starting Nov. 29. The first charge lands within three days of that date, and a second follows after Dec. 24. Fees come out of USDC first and then other assets. Accounts holding less than the fee would lose the entire balance, the emails say. Anyone who withdraws everything before Nov. 29 pays nothing. Binance had not published those fee figures in a public announcement as of Sunday, so the details rest on the customer emails, not an official notice. The company’s spokesperson confirmed only the closure date and the restriction of services. The four countries share one trait: Binance ran locally registered businesses in each before the MiCA transition ended. Its first outreach to users there came in June, when it urged them to withdraw. A license Binance still has not won MiCA requires crypto firms to win authorization in one EU member state before serving customers across the bloc. Binance withdrew its Greek license application in June and said it would seek approval elsewhere, without naming the country. Reuters had reported that month that Greece’s Hellenic Capital Market Commission was poised to reject the bid, as Bitcoin Magazine reported . As the MiCA deadline arrived, the EU’s securities regulator also ordered unlicensed crypto firms to exit the market. Binance told users at the time that it remained committed to Europe. It does not appear on the European Securities and Markets Authority’s register of authorized crypto providers, and it has not said which regulator now holds its application. business.title: U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place. The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020. That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more. It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. Why the agencies backed off Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels. Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995. Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it. The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment. The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.” What the withdrawal does and does not do The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule. What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. sports.title: Blades Brown’s Win Proves 19-year-olds Can Beat The Best Right Now
sports.description: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images Golf history just got rewritten by a teenager who refused to quit. Blades Brown, just 19 years old, captured his first PGA Tour title on Sunday in Mexico. He did something no one has done in 95 years. The win came after he erased a seven-stroke deficit in the final round against Ben James. This isn’t just a lucky break for a kid. It is a statement that the future of the game is here and it is aggressive. The Comeback That Shocked Everyone Most players would have folded with that kind of hole in the standings. Brown did not even blink. He closed with a nine-under 63 to force a playoff, according to the Associated Press. The final score was 23-under 265, which cleared a logjam of eight players who were all within a single stroke of one another. On the second sudden-death hole, a four-foot birdie putt secured the victory for him. Brown is now the fourth-youngest winner in tour history. He bypassed college entirely to turn pro out of high school, a move that paid off instantly. “It hasn’t set in just yet, I guess, the magnitude of being a PGA Tour winner,” Brown said in a statement reported by Yahoo Sports . That lack of shock is exactly what makes this win so dangerous for the rest of the field. He has been thinking about this day since he was five years old. Now he is living it. At the 2023 U.S. Amateur, the kid broke a 103-year-old record, joining Tiger Woods as the only players to win the U.S. Junior Amateur and be the medalist in the U.S. Amateur in the same year. Success at this age is not an accident. Why The Old Guard Should Worry Ben James fought hard but fell short. James held a four-shot lead after 54 holes before the game got away from him on Sunday. He still managed to force the playoff with a clutch eagle on the 18th hole. James hit a 285-yard shot into 20 feet and made the putt to salvage a 70. “Had a feeling that it was going to go in,” James said of his eagle putt, per the Associated Press. But he missed an eight-foot putt on the second playoff hole while Brown made his three-footer. Last season, James held the number one spot in the PGA Tour University ranking, but he failed to stop the younger talent. The combined age of these two players in the playoff was 42, the youngest in tour history. This signals a shift in who wins on Sunday. A Masters berth is nearer for Brown at 54th globally, provided he ends the season within the top 50. Brown said with a huge grin, according to Yahoo Sports, “I’m just so obsessed with this game,”. That obsession is the difference maker. That obsession proves experience does not always beat hunger when the pressure is highest.

sports.title: Kyle Whittingham Reveals What Finally Convinced Him to Fire Jason Beck
sports.description: Michigan Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham has finally revealed exactly what pushed him to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck , and apparently, it took one final look at the film to seal the deal. Speaking to reporters on Monday, Whittingham explained that he initially planned to wait until the conclusion of the 2026 season before making any major changes to his offensive coaching staff. However, after reviewing the film from Michigan’s embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State, he realized waiting was no longer an option. According to Brad Galli of WXYZ-TV , Whittingham pointed directly to the regression he witnessed against the Spartans as the reason for his sudden change of heart. The Michigan head coach also made something else perfectly clear: Nobody pressured him into firing Beck. Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham looks up at the scoreboard during second half action at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Michigan State won the game 15-6. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kyle Whittingham Reveals What Changed His Mind About Jason Beck During Monday’s press conference, Whittingham explained that watching Saturday’s game on film convinced him that an immediate coaching change was necessary. “When I turned the film on and really dove into it, it just became apparent to me that I needed to make the change now, and there’s just too much regression in the offense in that particular game, and that’s what led to the decision,” Whittingham said. That explanation is particularly interesting considering what Whittingham said immediately following Saturday’s loss. At the time, he suggested he would evaluate his coaching staff after the season rather than make an immediate change. But apparently, the film told a different story. Whittingham also addressed whether outside pressure played any role in his decision to part ways with Beck, who followed him from Utah to Michigan. “ Zero outside influence. Just my own analysis, my own feel, my own gut instinct ,” Whittingham said. Those comments leave little room for interpretation. Despite growing frustration among Michigan fans and mounting criticism of the offense, Whittingham insists the decision was entirely his own. Michigan’s Offensive Struggles Became Impossible to Ignore The numbers from Saturday’s loss to Michigan State were nothing short of disastrous for the Wolverines. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Alabama Crimson Tide returned to national championship talk after a hard-fought victory at LSU. Alabama proved they belong among the top contenders for the national title. LSU moved the ball well but failed to score when it mattered most. The Tigers gained 457 total yards but could not convert those gains into enough points to beat Alabama. This specific breakdown in execution cost LSU the game and kept Alabama in the hunt for a big prize in January. A Win Despite the Numbers The box score tells a strange story for a team that won by 18 points. Despite securing 27 first downs and 380 passing yards, LSU suffered a crushing defeat. Alabama only had 285 total yards in the game. The Tide defense made key plays at the right moments to overcome this yardage gap. Alabama won the turnover battle and forced LSU to fail on every single fourth-down attempt. Lane Kiffin, the head coach for LSU, explained the issue after the game. “We didn’t make any. 0-for-4,” Kiffin said, according to a report . This inability to finish drives was the main reason LSU lost. The Tigers had chances to put points on the board but settled for field goals or turned the ball over. Alabama capitalized on these mistakes to build a lead they did not relinquish. Quarterback Growth Under Pressure Keelon Russell answered the biggest questions about the Alabama offense with his performance. He is a young quarterback who walked into a hostile stadium against a team ranked high in sacks and pressure. Pressure was exactly what beat Alabama against Tennessee in a previous game. LSU had the personnel to run that same blueprint to slow the Tide down. Russell stood in the pocket anyway and made the plays needed to win. This growth is the kind of development a team needs to make a deep run in the postseason. The bye week also helped the team look healthier and more physical. Alabama looked sharper than the version that played Tennessee. Ryan Coleman-Williams and other players who were injured stepped up to help the unit. The team showed it could handle adversity on the road. The Road to the Championship Alabama now sits right back in the conversation for the national championship. The team has the upside to beat anybody, including the top-ranked Georgia Bulldogs. Georgia remains the best team in the country, but Alabama has the talent to beat them on any given Saturday. If a few calls break Alabama’s way in a potential matchup, the Tide probably beats Georgia. This LSU win served as proof that the team can win games they are outgained in. The Lakers originally sold the jersey in December 2017 as part of a $20,000 package that included a signed No. 24 team-issued jersey. The No. 8 jersey’s latest price alone is 91.5 times the original package’s purchase price. The sale further strengthens The Realest’s reputation in the sports memorabilia market, coming after its $2.05 million auction of Shohei Ohtani’s game-worn Dodgers jersey from his MLB debut in Japan. technology.title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
technology.description: Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That's the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets , including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories. The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the "Yes, and don't ask again" option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local ".claude/settings.local.json" file on the user's computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it. This isn't really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user's local machine (assuming that machine doesn't become compromised itself, of course). And Anthropic notes in its Claude Code documentation that this particular settings file gets added to the developer's global .gitignore list , which usually prevents it from being shared publicly. technology.title: Machine learning researchers build a better world model
technology.description: Machine learning researchers have developed a technique that allows world models to make better predictions about how objects will behave. World models are used to train physical AI systems like robots how to navigate the real world. They predict the consequences of actions. But they do so based on observed data. These models could provide better direction to robots if they were able to make inferences about possible actions without being trained for all the possible outcomes. Randall Balestriero (Brown University, AMI Labs), Kerda Varaku, and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun (NYU, AMI Labs) describe an approach that might allow that to happen in a pre-print paper, "Counterfactual World Models: Natura Non Facit Saltus." The Latin refers to Gottfried Leibniz's axiom " nature makes no leaps ," which had a good run until it ran headlong into quantum mechanics. Yet for the authors, the saying explains how they have been able to devise a method for zero-shot physics inference. Counterfactual world models, said Balestriero in an email to The Register use "the mismatch between your prediction and the real world to figure out what did you get wrong, and from that you can better understand what happened for better future predictions, debugging, reasoning, all at test time." Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture ( JEPA ) models, developed by LeCunn and colleagues back in 2023, have been proposed for robots because they can take an action as input and ask what the world would be like with that action. But a JEPA world model produces an average of outcomes and would not be able to anticipate counterfactual scenarios – events that didn't happen. The technique that the researchers developed is not specific to JEPAs – it can be applied to any world model that predicts the average next state under any action. But JEPA models are particularly well suited to being adapted. Balestriero said that the counterfactual world model experiments were done using off-the-shelf encoders (DINOv2 and MAE) without any fine-tuning and only a small predictor trained on top. Creating a counterfactual world model from that starting point would only require minor additions. Counterfactual world models predict alternative scenarios more effectively by inferring possibilities from what did occur. "In causal inference, answering 'What would have happened had I acted differently?' takes three steps," explained Balestriero. "You use what you observed to learn something about those hidden factors, you change the action, and you predict again with the hidden factors kept exactly as they were. "Our counterfactual world model does all three steps with one subtraction." Balestriero cited an example from the paper: a boat crossing a river with a hidden current and how the JEPA world model and counterfactual world model predicted the boat's movements. "The world model predicted where the boat would end up after steering left, and it actually ended up two meters further downstream," he explained.

technology.title: Microsoft takes three decades to make Sticky Keys less sticky
technology.description: Windows testers are getting a new option in the Sticky Keys and Filter Keys dialogs – one to banish the pop-ups without needing to venture deep into Settings. It's only taken several decades for Microsoft to put the off switch where the interruption actually happens. The accessibility features themselves are useful, though triggering their activation prompts by accident is another matter. Once enabled, Sticky Keys let users press modifier keys (such as Control) one at a time instead of holding them down together. For example, rather than holding Control and pressing C to copy, a user can press and release Control, then press C. Filter Keys, meanwhile, ignores brief or repeated keystrokes and adjusts the keyboard's repeat behavior. However, the dialogs are of little use to people who don't need the features, and they can pop up at the most inconvenient moments. Tap Shift five times, and you'll see what we mean: Windows chimes and shows a dialog asking whether you'd like to turn on Sticky Keys. Dismiss it, hit Shift five times, and there it is again. Or hold down the right Shift key for eight seconds to be treated to the Filter Keys pop-up. You can stop this behavior elsewhere in the system, but it requires a trek through Windows settings. The change, introduced in the Experimental Windows Insider Build 26340.9882, adds an option to the Sticky Keys or Filter Keys dialogs to dismiss the prompts permanently. It's a small change, but one that should spare users an irritating interruption. Better late than never – even if "never ask me again" has taken roughly three decades to reach the dialog. Former Microsoft engineer Charles Opperman said he wrote the dialog in early 1995 "after @bradsilverberg kids kept activating StickeyKeys [sic] while playing Space Cadet pinball." Opperman added that a link to Settings was added in Windows 98 or what would become Windows 2000, and a checkbox was considered even then, but it wasn't deemed a priority. Users could turn off the prompt via settings. Now the option is front and center. The option is also rolling out in the Windows Insider Beta channel , although Microsoft has not announced a general release date. ®

science.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
science.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . "An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable." The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain. "The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said. science.description: null So, you thought "Stranger Things" was done and dusted after all that Conformity Gate nonsense? No way! Netflix's sci-fi sensation returns in the live-action prequel series "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure." Created by the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry, with the episodes set to be directed by Joe Wright ("Darkest Hour", "Black Mirror"), this new show isn't set in Hawkins or the electric '80s. No, this time around, the action takes place in Marion, Nevada, in 1955, and you know what else is located in Nevada, right? Area 51 . The teaser trailer certainly teases the possibility of a trip to the world's most paradoxically famous secret military base, showcasing a bike and radio resting outside of a fence with a sign that clearly says it's a restricted area (in any TV show or film, that's actually an invitation to see what's on the other side). Of course, the tease doesn't end there, as the thunder booms in the sky and there's a visual hint of a wormhole. No story details about "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" have been released to date, but there are some clues out there for all the Internet sleuths. Trefrey wrote the Henry Creel-focused "Stranger Things: The First Shadow" play, while Matt Duffer explained to Variety how a spin-off show would tackle the rock that Henry found in the briefcase in "Stranger Things." So, yes, expect this to be a Henry-centric affair and the start of his long, hard road to hell and becoming Vecna. (Image credit: Netflix) What'll be interesting, though, is to see how the show ties into the history of Area 51. After all, it was on April 12, 1955, that CIA officer Richard Bissell discovered the site, while the "Other Worlds" trailer has the date of April 19th clearly marked onscreen, so the timelines align nicely here. "Stranger Things" has never been shy of tying itself to real-world science and historical events, so it'll be fascinating to see how the show explores Area 51 as a concept and the secrets everybody believes are hidden there. Was it really a site to test highly advanced weapons and aircraft, or was E.T. 's cousin held hostage there until he revealed Colonel Sanders' 11 herbs and spices? Who knows, with all this renewed excitement around this mysterious military facility, we might get another "Storm Area 51" event to enjoy and laugh at all over again. Regardless, more "Stranger Things" is welcome news, and since it's presumably about one of the show's best characters, Henry Creel, it only adds another layer to his already intriguing lore. If we can't have an origin story about Hopper's incredible and envious moustache, this is the next best thing. "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" arrives on Netflix in 2028. science.description: NASA’s two ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft have each successfully completed a powered Earth flyby, using Earth’s gravity in combination with a sustained engine burn to slingshot themselves toward Mars. With these successful maneuvers complete, the twin spacecraft are on target to reach the Red Planet in September 2027. “This is the first time NASA has used a powered Earth flyby to propel a spacecraft toward Mars, and we’ve now executed this maneuver twice, flawlessly, in just two days,” said Asal Naseri, acting associate flight director for the Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video In November 2026, each of NASA’s two ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft executed a powered flyby of Earth, combining Earth’s gravity with an engine burn, to slingshot itself toward Mars. The first spacecraft made its closest approach around 5 a.m. EST on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the second did so two days later, around 6 a.m. EST on Monday, Nov. 9. In this animation, each spacecraft’s approximately 9-minute trans-Mars injection burn appears as an orange arc along the spacecraft’s trajectory. So instead of heading straight for the Red Planet, as most other Mars missions have done, both spacecraft entered a “loiter” or “Earth-proximity” orbit. They charted a first-of-its-kind, kidney-bean-shaped course around a place in space about a million miles from Earth called Lagrange point 2, which is a gravitational balancing point on the opposite side of Earth from the Sun. science.title: Meteorite that landed in Cape Cod was a 'lone wolf' from the outer solar system, scientists find
science.description: Thanks to a combination of radar, infrasound, dash-cam and security camera footage, astronomers have tracked the bright daytime meteor that fell over Cape Cod Bay in May 2026 back to its origin as a small asteroid perturbed by Jupiter and sent on a comet-like orbit towards Earth. Meteor fireballs visible in the daytime are referred to as 'bolides'. At 1:06 p.m. local time (18:06 UTC) on May 30, 2026 one such bolide was widely witnessed falling out of the sky over coastal Massachusetts, with members of the public also reporting an associated sonic boom that rumbled across the north-eastern coast of the United States. Now, a team of scientists from Europe and the United States, led by space physicist Juha Vierinen of the Arctic University of Norway in Tromsø, have patched together measurements from a meteor-observing radar network, regular weather radar, infrasound stations and camera footage to fully characterize the fall of this meteoroid and trace its orbit around the sun . Key to these observations were measurements by the Spread Spectrum Interferometric Meteor Observing Network (SIMONe) based at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's (MIT's) Haystack Observatory. SIMONe is a project jointly developed by MIT, the Arctic University of Norway and the Leibniz Institute of Atmospheric Physics in Kühlungsborn, Germany. "We were fortunate that the event occurred within the coverage of SIMONe," Vierinen told Space.com. This is echoed by Ryan Volz, a radio scientist at Haystack Observatory who is a member of the team who studied the May 30 bolide. "We got pretty lucky to observe this one," Volz told Space.com. "A bolide like this would have to enter the atmosphere within about 62 miles (100 kilometers) of a SIMONe-like meteor radar system for the head echoes we saw to be detectable, and there are only a handful of places in the world that currently meet that criteria." A head echo is what radar sees when a meteoroid – what we call the lump of rock that becomes a meteor while it is still in space – enters Earth's atmosphere , generating a cloud of plasma around it as it superheats the atmosphere and its outer surface. "The head echoes give the best constraints on the meteoroid's trajectory," said Volz. The existence of the head echo is usually very brief, taking place at 56 miles (90 kilometers () altitude down to about 44 miles (71 kilometers) when the plasma around the meteoroid is dense enough to return a radar echo. The head echo transitions into a 'trail echo', which is produced by a streak of turbulent plasma that is left in the wake of the meteoroid after it has passed through a given part of the atmosphere. In the case of the 30 May bolide, the trail echo was detected down to an unusually low altitude of 20 miles (32 kilometers), at which point the falling rock fragmented with an explosive force equivalent to 500 tons of TNT, whereas the total impact energy of the bolide was in the region on 1.1 kilotons of TNT. science.title: NASA unveils $10 billion in moon base contracts, new lunar missions and the 'PROMISE' of a nuclear-powered rover
science.description: null CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA is pushing ahead with its plan to build a moon base for astronauts by 2032, with the agency unveiling up to $10 billion in contracts to launch and deliver cargo to the moon and other efforts on Saturday (Nov. 7). The NASA announcement, revealed here during the space agency's "Max Power" air show event at Kennedy Space Center , included plans for a new $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) framework, dubbed CLPS 2, about$1.3 billion in funding for the agency's Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) program, and the nuclear-powered "PROMISE" rover on the moon. The announcements mark another step in NASA's effort to establish infrastructure on the moon before Artemis astronauts return to its surface, including a rover and other cargo and research elements. "Under the current CLPS contract, it's all all or nothing, which might be fine if you're only doing one or two of those [missions] per year," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman told Space.com during a press conference on Saturday. "But when you're trying to scale up to what we're talking about today, you want to have the flexibility to move pieces around." Landing cargo on the moon NASA selected eight companies to compete for the new CLPS 2 missions under the framework: Blue Origin , Firefly Aerospace, Intuitive Machines, ispace-U.S., Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, SpaceX and Voyager Technologies. The contracts for the 10-year CLPS 2 architecture carry a combined maximum value of $10 billion, rather than $10 billion in immediately awarded missions. NASA also increased the ceiling of its existing CLPS contract from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion to support the agency's "Phase One" Moon Base objectives. NASA is also following through on a promise Isaacman made in June, when he proposed repurposing an engineering model of the Perseverance and Curiosity Mars rovers (essentially an Earth-based twin) as a mission-ready rover to send to the moon. NASA awarded Blue Origin a $94 million base contract, with an additional $140 million option period based on performance, to deliver PROMISE to the lunar surface aboard its Blue Moon Mark 1 lander .
